definition: Quantum natural language processing (QNLP) is the application of quantum computing to natural language processing (NLP).
details: It computes word embeddings as parameterised quantum circuits that can solve NLP tasks faster than any classical computer. It is inspired by categorical quantum mechanics and the DisCoCat framework, making use of string diagrams to translate from grammatical structure to quantum processes.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Quantum natural language processing — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
